topic: Economic Design of Smart-Contract Carbon Pools: Participation, Value Allocation, and Upstream Transmission in Biochar Supply Chains
central_object: executable fee, transaction and allocation rules; not a generic blockchain benefit term

research_questions.RQ1: How do inventory-dependent fees and execution rules shape participation and routing?
research_questions.RQ2: How should a designer choose economic rules under composition and budget constraints?
research_questions.RQ3: When does monetization transmit into producer income and physical supply?

default_baseline: Gate20 partial venue allocation with fixed initial state, exogenous prices, enforceable procurement rights and contractual beta
designer_scope: Gate21 known-state depositFeeScale choice in a 30-value approved menu; normative output objective, assumed HHI limit and recipient token budget
commitment: one-horizon commitment assumed; not implied by owner permissions
conditional_contrast: Gate19 all-output routing can reduce output; this is not robust to Gate20 partial allocation and is not the general headline
open_questions: full historical proxy-upgrade and contract-version census beyond sampled versions
global continuous or function-space fee optimum with participation and budget constraints
